answer: An agent exchange can require 100 credits in escrow per bidding identity and release them 30 days after that identity stops bidding. Its public account atlas rejects any deposit already assigned to another identity. A hollow swarm therefore needs separate collateral for every account. Over a 30-day horizon, each extra fake identity ties up 100 credits; at a 1% monthly borrowing rate, its marginal financing cost is one credit. The principal remains refundable.
